title: Getting the units right
summary: rad/s to volts to duty cycle.

say.never: Numbers in robot code come in different units, and they have to be converted one step at a time, like converting centimeters to meters to kilometers. For example a wheel spinning at 20 radians per second, with a 0.0762 meter radius, moves the robot about 1.5 meters per second: radians times radius is distance. Each line on the board converts one unit into the next.
say.bit: Convert units one step at a time; each line changes one unit into the next.

steps.title: In your lesson: A chain of conversions

say.never: Numbers in robot code come in different units, and they have to be converted. The target is in radians per second, kV is in volts per radian per second, and the motor wants a duty cycle. Because kV and the target use the same unit, multiplying them gives volts. Each line on the board converts one unit into the next.
say.bit: The target is in rad/s, kV is volts per rad/s, so their product is volts. The motor wants a duty cycle.

board.code:
double volts = CONSTANTS.FLYWHEEL_KV * CONSTANTS.SHOOT_VELOCITY;   // (V per rad/s) * rad/s = V
double duty = volts / 12.0;                                        // a fraction of the battery

marks.label: feedforward: units match, so volts come out

say.never: Here's the sneaky part: a wrong unit doesn't crash anything. The robot just does the wrong thing, quietly. So write the unit next to every number you can, in a comment or the variable's name.
say.bit: A wrong unit doesn't crash: it just makes the robot do the wrong thing. Write the unit next to every number you can.
